response.query: Which force fields and solvent models (examples: Amber ff19SB/OPC, CHARMM36m/TIP3P) produce the best agreement for small de novo folds and should be committed to for pilot MD validation?
response.answer: For small de novo folds, the AMBER ff19SB force field with OPC water model shows best agreement for pilot MD validation. CHARMM36m with TIP3P also performs well for some proteins.

results.title: Scrutinizing the protein hydration shell from molecular dynamics simulations against consensus small-angle scattering data | Communications Chemistry
results.content: To this end, we carried out simulations using 18 different combinations of protein force field and water model (Table S1), computed SAS curves taking explicit solvent into account18."),27."),28."),29."),30."), and compared the derived *R*g values to consensus SAS data from the round-robin study (Table S2)26."). Next, we studied the effect of 18 different combinations of force fields for protein and water on the hydration shell, as quantified by Δ*R*g and \(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\) values. Figure 3b, d, f presents \(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\) values obtained from SAXS relative to SANS/D2O for the proteins RNaseA, xylanase, and glucose isomerase, computed with 18 different combinations of force fields for protein and water and using unrestrained simulations. Interestingly, variations among different force fields do not follow the same trend for glucose isomerase as observed for the near-neutral proteins RNaseA or xylanase; for instance, CHARMM36m simulations yield similar (with TIP3P) or even larger (with SPC/E or OPC3) \(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\) values as compared to the simulations with the AMBER force fields ff14SB or ff99SB-ildn. Figure 4 summarizes Δ*R*g and \(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\) values for five proteins, obtained as a consensus average over six combinations of protein force field and water model (Methods), which exhibited good agreement with experimental data according to Fig. 3b, d, f. Overall, we found remarkable agreement between \(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\) from MD simulations and experiments for many combinations of protein force field and water model for the proteins RNaseA, xylanase, and glucose isomerase. For the electrically nearly neutral proteins xylanase and RNaseA, simulations with CHARMM36m typically underestimated \(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\) as compared to experimental values, in particular together with the widely used TIP3P or cTIP3P water models, indicative of underestimated hydration shell contrasts. As readout of the hydration shell structure, we focused on the difference in *R*g values from SAXS relative to SANS experiments in D2O (\(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\)), which we computed from MD simulations with explicit-solvent SAS calculations to enable quantitative comparison with experimental SAS data. For many force fields, \(\Delta {R}\_{{{{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}}}}}^{{{{{{{{\rm{SAS}}}}}}}}}\) values from MD simulations revealed excellent agreement with consensus SAS data from a recent worldwide round-robin study26."), suggesting that simulations accurately capture the hydration shell contrast relative to the bulk.

results.title: The Amber Force Fields
results.content: The ff19SB force field contains amino-acid specific backbone parameters. ff14SBonlysc  In the  ff14SBonlysc force field, the side-chain dihedral parameters were fit to quantum mechanical data for each amino acid. If you want a 3-point water model to minimize computational cost, this is a good choice  ff14SB  The ff14SB force field is intended for use with the **TIP3P water model**. Specialized Protein Force Fieldsff15ipq (including fluorinated aromatic amino acids)  The ff15ipq force field is an implicitly polarized force field that was developed with a self-consistent physical model and rebuilds nearly all charge, angle, torsion, and some van-der Waals parameters for proteins. The force field also includes parameters for fluorinated aromatic amino acids. Recently, OPC water model in combination with the ff99SB force field was found to improve significantly the accuracy of atomistic simulations of IDPs.Other protein force fieldsSee the **Sections 3.1.3 - 3.1.5** of the  Amber Reference Manual for more information.- fb15 ("force balance") - Duan et al.

results.title: Comparison of Charge Models for Fixed-Charge Force Fields:  Small-Molecule Hydration Free Energies in Explicit Solvent | The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
results.content: Comparison of Charge Models for Fixed-Charge Force Fields:  Small-Molecule Hydration Free Energies in Explicit Solvent. # Comparison of Charge Models for Fixed-Charge Force Fields:  Small-Molecule Hydration Free Energies in Explicit Solvent Click to copy article linkArticle link copied! In molecular simulations with fixed-charge force fields, the choice of partial atomic charges influences numerous computed physical properties, including binding free energies. Here, we compute hydration free energies for a set of 44 small, neutral molecules in two different explicit water models (TIP3P and TIP4P-Ew) to examine the influence of charge model on agreement with experiment. Surprisingly, agreement with experimental hydration free energies does not increase substantially with increasing level of quantum theory, even when the quantum calculations are performed with a reaction field treatment to better model the aqueous phase.
